column1: # ---- 03-contracts/C0 and C1 ----
A contract is the complete, closed description of what crosses a seam: if it is not in the field table, it does not cross.
There is no additional-context parameter, no object and no dictionary of extras in any contract.
A contract is a value: immutable record types and readonly structs, with no references to mutable state, no handles into another layer's storage and no delegates.
A contract is serialisable and round-trips to a stable binary and a stable JSON form.
Serialisability is what makes seam recording and per-layer golden tests possible.
Every payload carries schemaVersion, and a consumer rejects a version it does not understand rather than guessing.
Every payload carries contentHash of itself and inputHashes of the payloads that produced it, forming the Merkle chain.
Every contract documents its fields in a table with the columns Field, Type, Unit, Card., Range, Null, Default, MaxStale and Notes.
The Type column names the typed quantity and not a primitive.
The Unit column is explicit even when implied by the type.
Cardinality is one of 1, [H] per slot, [S,H] per scenario and slot, [B] per block, or 0..1 optional.
A value outside the declared Range is a contract failure.
The Default column carries the conservative default, or an em dash if none exists.
MaxStale is the maximum age before quality degrades, expressed in SlotSpan.
A field with Null = yes must have either a Default or a documented escalation, and a nullable field with no defined behaviour on absence is an incomplete contract.
The universal invariants are applied at every seam by a shared validator invoked on both sides.
No numeric field contains NaN or infinity.

Every numeric field has a declared unit in its field table; dimensioned quantities use a typed quantity while dimensionless fields may be double or int but must be declared with an em dash in the Unit column and range-constrained, and a dimensioned field typed as a bare double is a violation.
schemaVersion is recognised by the consumer.
contentHash matches the payload, and inputHashes are present and non-empty.
No payload contains a wall-clock timestamp taken at construction.
All slot-indexed arrays have the length declared by horizon.
All scenario-indexed arrays share the scenario axis length and ordering.
asOf is non-decreasing across successive payloads on the same seam.
Every field marked Null = no is present.
Declared ranges hold for every element, not merely the first.
Validation is on by default in every environment, including production.
Validation costs a few microseconds against a solve measured in milliseconds.
Each seam is validated twice: the producer validates before emitting and the consumer validates on receipt.
A producer-side validation failure enters the producing layer's degradation ladder.
A consumer-side validation failure goes to HALT, because a contract violation means the producer is in an unknown state and nothing downstream can be trusted.
An additive change — a new optional field with a default — is a minor version bump and old consumers keep working.
Removing a field, changing a type, changing a unit, changing a semantic or tightening a range is a major version bump, and the consumer must be updated in the same commit.
Unit changes are always major, even when the type is unchanged, because a field silently moving from EUR/MWh to EUR/kWh is the archetypal catastrophic change.
A contract change requires the doc, the version and the conformance tests in one commit.
Fields subject to data quality carry a parallel quality channel rather than embedding quality in the value.
A QualityStamp carries provenance, quality, knowledgeTime, sourceId and maxStaleBreached.
A QualityStamp is carried per series where quality is uniform across the array and per element where it is not, such as a forecast with a measured prefix and a forecast suffix.
Consumers map quality to risk parameters and never to branches.
Every payload carries tickId as (SlotId, clock, sequence), which identifies the tick uniquely.
Every payload carries asOf, the knowledge-time boundary for every fact inside it.
Every payload carries horizon as a SlotSpan, assetId for the battery, poiId for the connection point, and manifestId as the run manifest hash.
Multi-asset is not in scope for v1, but assetId and poiId are present in every contract from the start so that adding a second asset is not a schema break.
C1 carries the BeliefSnapshot payload at version 1.0 from L1 to L2.
C1 carries everything Valuation may know about the world, as of a knowledge-time boundary, over the hot window, and nothing else reaches Valuation.
Valuation has no access to the Belief store, to the network, or to a clock.
The C1 envelope adds scenarioCount, the shared scenario axis length S; scenarioWeights, non-negative and summing to 1; slotStart, the first slot of the window; and slotCount, equal to H_hot.
socNow is measured, and if telemetry is lost the engine escalates rather than defaulting.
The operating band socMin to socMax includes warranty derates.
pMaxDischarge and pMaxCharge are per-slot and may derate on temperature or state of health.
sohFraction is informational, and derates flow through pMax* and socMax rather than through it.
poiImportLimit and poiExportLimit are the contractual and physical POI envelope, per slot.
auxLoad is explicit per slot and not folded into η, and its conservative default is the site maximum.
The conservative default for load is a high quantile, because a high load protects the peak.
The conservative default for pv is zero, because zero PV protects the peak.
loadQuality and pvQuality are per-element QualityStamps, carrying a measured prefix and a forecast suffix.
daPrice is scenario- and slot-indexed in EUR/MWh with range [-9999, 9999], and negative prices are legal and material.
daCleared is present only post-gate and null pre-gate.
idSpreadBelief is a half-spread belief whose wide default suppresses trading.
afrrCapPrice is per product block with a zero default, so the engine does not chase reserve revenue on invented prices.
activationUp and activationDn are fractions of committed MW in [0,1] and are scenario-consistent with prices.
imbalancePrice is a reBAP-type belief.
Every scenario-indexed array shares the axis, so index s denotes the same state of the world in load, pv, daPrice, activationUp and all others.
Violation of the shared scenario axis is a hard failure and not a warning.
idReliableVolumeBuy and idReliableVolumeSell are the volumes that may be counted on, defaulting to zero.
idVolumeByPriceBand is an optional refinement pending the fill-fidelity decision.
The liquidity beliefs are volumes only, with no price field, which is the C1-side enforcement of the rule that fill probability constrains the Planner but never prices for it.
Prices for quoting reach the quoting policy by a different route, outside C2.
activeRegimes is a non-empty list of TariffRegimeIds taken from the calendar.
peakPrice is carried per regime in EUR/kW/period and is non-negative.
leviesAndTaxes is a closed enumerated list of the non-reducible components, summed.
enfgLevies is the reducible EnFG components summed, charged on (21) and never on metered import.
isHlzf comes from the DSO HLZF table and its conservative default is true, inside the window.
awPositive and anzulegenderWert are derived in L1 §4.2.1 and not ingested.
awPositive carries (24)¼, is a realised parameter within the settled day-ahead horizon and scenario-indexed beyond it, and its conservative default of false forfeits the premium.
anzulegenderWert is AW, static per plant and EEG vintage.
zuordnungsFaktor is ZF, power-weighted, and sums to 1 across plants.
marktwertMonth is MW_month, derived per scenario from national spot and national solar generation on the shared axis, and never an independent series.
commonEegVintage is true only when every plant shares a § 51 or § 51b threshold, which is what makes the AW forfeit simultaneous and collapses A5 to A1, and false forbids the collapse.
The premium is MAX[anzulegenderWert − marktwertMonth; 0], which is convex in marktwertMonth.
marktwertMonth crosses as [S] rather than as a scalar because a point forecast understates the premium, most severely when AW and MW_month are close.
blockIndex maps each slot to its aFRR product block.
blockSlots carries the aFRR block lengths and comes from the calendar.
sustainDuration is the prequalification requirement D.
minBidMw and bidStepMw are the aFRR product granularity and are strictly positive.
symmetricProduct declares whether up and down reserve must be equal.
seriesQuality carries one QualityStamp per series and is the basis of the risk multiplier.
degradationMode is read from L0 and echoed in C1 so Valuation need not consult L0 separately.
criticalMissing is empty in NORMAL, and a non-empty criticalMissing implies a mode of at least DEFENSIVE.
socMin ≤ socNow ≤ socMax, and violation is a HALT because telemetry or the model is wrong.
No fact inside a BeliefSnapshot has knowledgeTime greater than asOf, and violation is a HALT for lookahead.
Every [H] array in C1 has length slotCount, and violation is a HALT.
blockIndex is non-decreasing and covers every slot exactly once, and violation is a HALT.
scenarioWeights are non-negative and sum to 1 within 1e-9, and violation is a HALT.
Reduced-ensemble marginal means match the full ensemble within tolerance, and violation warns and sets DEGRADED.
pMaxCharge and pMaxDischarge are non-negative and finite for every slot, and violation is a HALT.
etaCharge · etaDischarge ≤ 1, and violation is a HALT.
Every C1 field marked Null = no is present or is listed in criticalMissing, and otherwise the engine escalates per the ladder.
No handle, cursor or reference into the Belief store crosses C1.
No raw order-book data crosses C1; only the derived volume beliefs do.
No Planner or Settlement output crosses C1, because that arrives via L0 at a lag.
No wall-clock time crosses C1.
No model objects cross C1; only their evaluated outputs and their version hashes do.
